task.title: Strength reconciliation -999: root cause isolated below the Swift Task layer

result.summary: Build 64 Strength reconciliation acceptance failed again (Journey and Visible Abs photos now PASS on Build 64, Logged Today Cardio remains PASS -- Strength is the only remaining failed item). The new taskWasCancelledAtCatch diagnostic decisively shows Task.isCancelled was false at the exact catch site for the 2026-09-27 ~07:36 America/Los_Angeles confirm attempt, ruling out the SwiftUI/Swift-Task-cancellation theory with direct evidence. Correlated the exact attempt against the Server via two zero-write reads: command_receipts shows zero rows of any kind for this command type, ever, and in the tight window around the attempt the only receipts are two unrelated automatic HealthKit background-sync commands. The Server's own structured request/read log (pulled read-only) shows the app foregrounding (auth refresh + a burst of screen reads) at 14:34:39 UTC, the Founder opening the reconciliation review twice at 14:36:07 and 14:36:09 UTC, and then a 78-second total gap in server activity with zero trace of any commands-endpoint request before the next successful read at 14:37:27 UTC. security_events also shows zero rows in the window. Combined with a re-confirmed code read (no custom URLSession, no explicit cancellation, no session invalidation, no TaskGroup/race patterns anywhere in the app) and the discovery that the app has NO background-task-assertion (beginBackgroundTask/performExpiringActivity) anywhere for in-flight write requests, the most likely root cause consistent with every piece of evidence is that iOS cancelled the in-flight URLSessionTask at the OS level when the app was briefly backgrounded or interrupted during the confirm attempt -- a scenario made more likely because this exact command is characteristically triggered from a screen reached via a push notification tap, shortly after opening the app, unlike every other command type that succeeds reliably. No fix was implemented and no build was cut, per explicit instruction; a concrete next-candidate recommendation (wrap the command submission in a background-task assertion) is offered for whenever a fix is separately authorized.

zero_write_audit.summary: Two additional zero-write, owner-scoped, ROLLBACK-guaranteed production reads (command_receipts tight-window correlation plus a broader same-day/4-day activity comparison; security_events/sessions/devices check), both verified transaction_read_only=on before reading, both rolled back cleanly. Also pulled the Server's own structured runtime request/read log read-only via doctl apps logs (no database access, no mutation).

code_review.summary: Re-confirmed via direct code read that FounderServerAPI.swift's transport layer is unchanged since the prior diagnosis: plain URLSession.shared.data(for:) with no custom delegate/configuration, zero session invalidation calls, zero TaskGroup/race patterns anywhere in the app. Confirmed a genuinely new finding this pass: zero beginBackgroundTask/UIBackgroundTaskIdentifier/ProcessInfo.performExpiringActivity usage anywhere in the codebase, meaning no in-flight write request has any protection against the app backgrounding mid-request.

unexpected_findings: The app has zero background-task-assertion coverage anywhere for in-flight network write requests -- a real, previously-unnoticed architectural gap, not specific to reconciliation, though reconciliation's notification-driven trigger pattern makes it the command most likely to be affected in practice.

The Server's own structured runtime logs (via doctl apps logs) turned out to be a genuinely new, decisive correlation source beyond command_receipts -- they show successful reads (evidence-review-detail) immediately before the gap and prove the app's own command-logging path works clearly when a command DOES arrive, making the total silence for the reconciliation attempt unambiguous rather than merely absence-of-evidence.
backlog: Recommended next Native candidate: wrap the workout-reconciliation command submission (and any other write command reachable from a just-foregrounded/notification-driven screen) in a background-task assertion for the duration of the network call. Not implemented in this task -- offered for whenever separately authorized.

The reconciliation review's exact canonical_evidence_records collection_name/table was not located in this pass (searches under 'evidenceReviews' and an unfiltered collection search both returned empty) -- a minor, non-blocking gap; the core diagnosis did not depend on it.
Two ChatGPT master-thread-context handoffs remain unread in the inbox, staying scoped exactly to this task as instructed.
recommended_next_step: Do not request another Founder confirmation attempt. When ready, authorize the background-task-assertion fix as the next Strength candidate, with the same RED/GREEN + fresh-context-review standard already used in this lane.
